bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ 1` in `flatbuffers::EscapeString()` from the staged vulnerable checkout `b92bb0584d056cd237fa7059702e49617ee156b7`. After `monster_fuzzer` strips its first two control bytes, the witness is a Monster JSON object whose `flex` field is parsed through `Parser::ParseTable()`'s nested FlexBuffers builder with `BUILDER_FLAG_SHARE_ALL`. The first `flex` string decodes to 20 bytes and is inserted into the builder's shared-string pool with a 1-byte string-width. The second `flex` string decodes to 256 bytes, has the same first 20 bytes, and then an embedded NUL produced from `\u0000`; its `Value` therefore keeps `min_bit_width_ = BIT_WIDTH_16`. The vulnerable `StringOffsetCompare` uses `strncmp(..., min_len + 1)` with no length tie-break, so the second string is wrongly treated as equal to the first and reuses the first string's offset while keeping the second string's 2-byte width. `GenerateText()` later decodes `Monster.flex` as a nested flexbuffer, reaches the second vector element, reconstructs the string length with that stale 2-byte width, and `EscapeString()` reads one byte past the 1024-byte outer FlatBufferBuilder allocation copied from the malformed nested flexbuffer. The staged patch fixes the missing obligation by replacing the comparator with bytewise `memcmp()` plus an explicit length tie-break.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled `Monster.flex[0]` into the shared-string FlexBuffers builder state later reused by the bad deduplication.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` starts with control bytes `0x20 0x20`; `data[0] == 0x20` sets `opts.allow_non_utf8 = true` in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()`, and after those two bytes are stripped the payload begins `{flex:[...],name:""}`. The first quoted `flex` element decodes to 20 bytes and reaches this call unchanged.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `EscapeString()` trusts the corrupted length reconstructed for the second nested-flexbuffer string and dereferences one byte past the copied outer FlatBufferBuilder buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's ASan report records `READ of size 1` at `0x619000000980`, exactly 0 bytes past the 1024-byte region allocated while `Parser::ParseTable()` copied the malformed nested flexbuffer into the Monster buffer.

root_cause.description: The shared-string comparator stops at the first NUL and has no length tie-break, so a 256-byte string with an embedded NUL can compare equivalent to an earlier 20-byte prefix string. That lets `string_pool.find()` reuse the short string's offset for the long string.
root_cause.note: The staged patch replaces this with bytewise `memcmp()` plus `a.second < b.second` when the compared prefix bytes match. For the witness, the first string is 20 bytes and the second is 256 bytes with the same first 20 bytes and an embedded NUL at byte 21, so the vulnerable comparator collapses them incorrectly.

parser_admitted.description: The Monster schema marks field `flex` as `(flexbuffer)`, so once the post-flag payload is accepted as Monster JSON the parser routes the attacker-controlled `flex` value into a nested FlexBuffers builder with key and string sharing enabled.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the stale 2-byte width turns into the oversized string length later passed to `EscapeString()`: the reader consumes the wrong bytes before the reused short string and fabricates a larger `size_`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Step 7 leaves the second string reference with `u_` pointing at the first string's 1-byte-prefixed storage but `min_bit_width_ = BIT_WIDTH_16`. When step 11 reconstructs that string, `read_size()` uses `byte_width_ = 2` and therefore reads two bytes before the short string instead of its single-byte length prefix.

coarse_trace.summary: The Monster JSON witness enters the `flexbuffer` field parser, where a shared-string FlexBuffers builder stores the first 20-byte string and then receives a second 256-byte string containing an embedded NUL.

The vulnerable `StringOffsetCompare` collapses the 256-byte second string onto the earlier 20-byte string, reusing the short string's offset while leaving the second string's 2-byte width metadata intact.

The malformed nested flexbuffer bytes are copied into the outer Monster buffer and later re-entered by `GenerateText()` because `Monster.flex` is a nested flexbuffer field and `json_nested_flexbuffers` is enabled.
Printing the second nested-flexbuffer vector element reconstructs its string length with the stale 2-byte width, and `EscapeString()` overreads the 1024-byte outer FlatBufferBuilder allocation.

fine_trace.note: Inside the nested-flexbuffer parser for `Monster.flex`, the first array element from the post-flag payload is passed to the shared-string builder. Because the witness sets `opts.allow_non_utf8`, this first string reaches the builder as the original 20-byte byte sequence with no embedded NUL.

The first `flex` string is serialized as a FlexBuffer string with `len = 20`. `CreateBlob()` pushes a `Value` whose `min_bit_width_` is `WidthU(20) == BIT_WIDTH_8`, so this storage expects a 1-byte size prefix.
No equivalent string is in the pool yet, so the first string's `(offset,len)` pair is recorded in `string_pool`. This short, 1-byte-prefixed entry becomes the later dedup target.

When the parser reaches `flex[1]`, `attribute_` holds the decoded second string: 256 bytes long, the same first 20 bytes as step 1, and an actual `\0` at byte 21 produced from the JSON escape `\u0000`.

The second string is serialized as a new FlexBuffer string with `len = 256`. Its `Value` therefore keeps `min_bit_width_ = WidthU(256) == BIT_WIDTH_16`, meaning later readers will expect a 2-byte size prefix for this reference.

Root cause. `string_pool.find(so)` uses this comparator while checking step 5's `(offset, 256)` against the pool from step 3. `strncmp(..., min_len + 1)` stops at the embedded NUL / shorter terminator and treats the 20-byte first string and 256-byte second string as equivalent, with no length tie-break.

The duplicate-string branch fires. The freshly serialized 256-byte bytes are discarded, `u_` is replaced with the first string's offset from step 3, but the same `Value` still carries step 5's `min_bit_width_ = BIT_WIDTH_16`. The reference now points to 1-byte-prefixed storage while still advertising 2-byte string width.

After `builder.Finish()`, the malformed nested-flexbuffer bytes are copied into the outer Monster flatbuffer as the `flex:[ubyte]` field. ASan's allocation stack points at this outer `ForceVectorAlignment()` / `CreateVector()` copy, which is why the later overread lands in the 1024-byte FlatBufferBuilder allocation.

During text generation, the schema marks `Monster.flex` as `(flexbuffer)` and `json_nested_flexbuffers` defaults to true, so `GenerateText()` decodes the copied bytes as a nested flexbuffer and calls `root.ToString(...)` instead of dumping raw bytes.
The nested flexbuffer root is a two-element vector. After printing the first element, the loop reaches `i == 1` and dispatches `ToString()` on the corrupted second string reference from step 7.

Constructing `String(Indirect(), byte_width_)` for that second element immediately calls `read_size()`. Because the reference still carries `byte_width_ = 2` but the reused target string from step 2 was stored with a 1-byte size prefix, this read consumes the wrong bytes before the short string and manufactures an oversized `str.length()`.
The corrupted pointer/length pair from step 11 is handed straight to `EscapeString()` with no consistency check against the actual nested-flexbuffer buffer extent.

Sink. The loop trusts the corrupted length and dereferences one byte past the copied outer flatbuffer buffer. Stage 01's ASan report records `READ of size 1` at `0x619000000980`, exactly 0 bytes past the 1024-byte allocation created in step 8.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch replaces the vulnerable comparator with length-aware `memcmp()` and an explicit length tie-break, which matches the root cause reconstructed above. Stage 02 did not run the fixed build, so `patch_resolves` remains false here.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is the outer FlatBufferBuilder buffer that copies the malformed nested flexbuffer into `Monster.flex`. The root cause is earlier: nested FlexBuffers string dedup reuses the short string's offset while preserving the long string's width metadata, which later causes the overread inside that copied allocation.

format.name: monster_fuzzer control bytes plus Monster JSON
format.contract: The exact witness begins with two fuzzer control bytes, `0x20 0x20`, so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` strips them and sets `opts.allow_non_utf8 = true`. The remaining payload is a Monster JSON object with `flex:[S1,S2]` and `name:""`, where `S1` decodes to exactly 20 bytes (`40 40 87 87 87 62 2c 2c 34 ff ff ff ff ff 40 bf 40 40 50 40`) and `S2` decodes to exactly 256 bytes whose first 20 bytes are exactly `S1`, whose byte 21 is `00` (spelled `\u0000` in the JSON text), and whose remaining bytes are the witness's trailing padding bytes. That exact 20-byte/256-byte pair makes the share-all FlexBuffers builder store `S1` with a 1-byte string width, then wrongly deduplicate `S2` onto `S1`'s offset while keeping `S2`'s 2-byte width. `GenerateText()` must then reach the nested `flex` vector's second element and call `EscapeString()` on the resulting corrupted string reference.
